context: Given the strictly increasing array nums = [1, 3, 6, 8, 12, 15, 23, 26, 31, 35], with indices 0 through 9, find target = 6.
description: The upper panel, “Represent the array as a bar chart,” shows ten vertical bars increasing in height from left to right. Each bar has its element value at the top. The indices 0 through 9 appear below the bars under the label “Index.” The lower panel shows the same array as ten adjacent cells in a row. A double-headed arrow connects the panels to show that the bar chart and the one-dimensional array represent exactly the same data.

Both the bar chart and the array cells highlight the value 6 at index 2 in teal. To its left, indices 0 and 1 hold the smaller values 1 and 3. To its right, indices 3 through 9 hold the larger values 8, 12, 15, 23, 26, 31, and 35, respectively. This figure introduces the input and target before binary search begins halving the interval.

frames.explanation: A successful search should return index 2, where the target appears.
frames.title: Sample input for binary search

summary: A bar chart and a row of array cells show the same sorted array and search target.
